one_liner: Copper CRM has a broad REST Developer API using API-key headers, but no free tier: API needs a Professional plan or a 14-day trial, and OAuth app registration requires emailing Copper. An official MCP server is announced but still in waitlist beta.
auth_notes: API key is generated in System settings > API Keys (admin only) and sent with X-PW-AccessToken, X-PW-Application and X-PW-UserEmail headers. OAuth 2.0 exists but app registration requires contacting partners@copper.com, so it isn't self-serve. developer.copper.co and getcopper.io describe different products and were ignored.
access_notes: No free plan. Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial, no credit card required, and the trial includes API access. Basic has no API; Professional and Business include it.
blocker_notes: API needs Professional or higher, or the 14-day trial, which is short for ongoing toolkit testing. Self-serve OAuth is not available because app registration goes through partners@copper.com.

evidence.quote: There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0. API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations.
Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial, and no credit card is required.
The free trial grants temporary access to Professional and Business-level features, including the API
Copper Basic and Starter do not include API access.
The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.
Yes. Copper is launching an official MCP server, built and hosted by Copper. The beta launches in November 2026.
Request early access to the beta, or join the waitlist for updates as we get closer to launch.
